title: Karniyarik
subtitle: Turkish aubergine stuffed with spiced minced lamb
excerpt: Fried aubergines filled with a rich mixture of minced lamb, tomato, pine nuts, and spices, then baked until the filling sets and the skins soften. A Turkish home classic.
sourceNotes: Classic Turkish stuffed aubergine; karniyarik means 'split belly'. Lamb mince is traditional; beef mince is also common in Turkish households.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The filling can be made a day ahead and refrigerated. Fry the aubergines and stuff them just before baking.

content.text: Karniyarik is a fried and baked aubergine dish with a meaty, spiced filling. The aubergines are partially fried before baking, which gives them the right texture. Watch the oil temperature when frying: too cool and the aubergines absorb oil and go greasy.

items.prepNote: half a tin, for the baking liquid

content.text: Peel strips from each aubergine to give a striped appearance. Cut a deep slit lengthways down the centre, leaving the ends intact. Salt the inside and leave to drain for 15 minutes, then pat dry.
Heat 3 tablespoons of oil in the frying pan over a medium-high heat. Fry the aubergines on all sides for 5 to 6 minutes until golden and slightly softened. Transfer to the roasting tin, cut side up.
Lower the heat to medium. Add the remaining oil and fry the pine nuts for 1 minute until lightly golden. Remove and set aside.
Add the onion to the pan and cook for 6 minutes until soft. Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute. Add the mince and cook, breaking it apart, for 8 minutes until browned.
Stir in the cumin, paprika, and cinnamon. Add the fresh tomatoes and tomato puree. Cook for 5 minutes until the sauce thickens. Season with salt and pepper. Stir in the parsley and pine nuts.
Heat the oven to 180C. Open the slit on each aubergine and spoon the filling in generously. Press it in firmly. Mix the tinned tomatoes with the water and pour around the aubergines.
Bake uncovered for 30 minutes until the aubergines are completely soft and the tops are lightly coloured. Rest for 10 minutes before serving with rice or bread.

items.symptom: The aubergines are greasy after frying.
items.cause: The oil was not hot enough before the aubergines went in.
items.fix: The oil should be shimmering before you add the aubergines. Pat them very dry after salting to reduce oil absorption.

items.symptom: The filling sits on top rather than inside the aubergine.
items.cause: The slit was not deep enough, or the flesh was too firm.
items.fix: Press the aubergine open with the back of a spoon to widen the pocket. If the flesh is still firm after frying, give it another 3 minutes in the pan.

items.symptom: The baking liquid dries out before the aubergines are done.
items.cause: The tin was too wide, or the oven runs hot.
items.fix: Add another splash of water to the tin and loosely cover with foil. Check after 10 more minutes.
